messages:
aj: heads-up — we just had a weird spike in iops on us-west2 scratch nodes during a mass tempfile cleanup. GPU provisioning stalled for ~6m.

maria: gah, that sounds like the janitor sweep again. any logs?

aj: pasting the janitor log tail:
```
I0305 04:10:13 janitor.go:412] deleting /tmp/scratch/gnode-12234/tmpdir_20260305_4032 (files=120k, size=22G)
E0305 04:10:13 cleaner.go:89] rmall failed: unlinkat: I/O error
W0305 04:10:14 io_throttle.go:75] io queue depth burst -> throttling, pending=512
```

aj: and the kube events for the gpu-provisioner: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x4 over 6m)  default-scheduler  binding failed: attach timeout waiting for ephemeral storage
```

maria: looks like the delete wave caused overlayfs syncs to pile up. when the scrub hits a hot stripe it spikes IO and the bdi writeback goes bonkers.

devon: @aj can you confirm which janitor revision ran? we shipped a cleanup concurrency bump last week.

aj: running `kubectl describe pod janitor-9f6f` shows image tag `redwood/janitor:2026.03.01-concurrency+2` — timestamp matches.

infra-bot: notice created: scratchpool-iops-alert (us-west2) — 1768459080 — 85% of ioq limit consumed

maria: that concurrency bump was intended for cold-path deletes, but apparently it doesn't respect per-node bucketization. It sprays deletes across all worker threads.

devon: short-term mitigation: can we rollback concurrency to previous value (1) and add a backoff in the janitor loop?

aj: I'm about to roll a config patch to flip `delete_concurrency=1` in the ConfigMap and restart janitor on a small canary set.

sre-oncall: please also throttle the scratchpool io quota for janitor pods to 50MB/s each, otherwise we'll keep stomping the scheduler.

devon: agree. patch suggestion: add randomized sleep(50-200ms) per 1000 files and exponentially backoff on IO errors. Also batch unlink into smaller chunks.

aj: applying canary now to 3 nodes in us-west2-a. `kubectl set env ds/janitor DELETE_CONCURRENCY=1 -n infra`

deploy-bot: Rolling update started for daemonset janitor (namespace: infra). 3/3 updated on canary subset.

aj: canaries look sane — iops on those nodes dropped 70% within 90s. provisioning queue cleared.

maria: good. medium-term we should add metric partitioning: tag deletes by device-hotness and prefer low-io devices first. Also telemetry: expose per-delete latency distribution so we can detect bad segments early.

devon: also adding a guard to avoid deletion waves during our GPU attach windows (00:00-06:00 UTC for us-west2). Scheduler should advertise attach windows to janitor via lease API.

aj: note for follow-up: we observed a small number (~12) of `unlinkat` I/O errors that correlate with contiguous read errors on one NVMe. SRE will open a drive-retire ticket if counts rise.

sre-oncall: opened ticket INF-2026-314 (retire-pool gn-12234) and flagged for SMART scan.

maria: cost note — throttling janitor increases ephemeral occupancy and may push some workloads to Dedicated (cost delta). track how many pods are waiting >5m.

aj: added a dashboard tile: "janitor backoff vs gpu attach waits" and a simple alert if attach_waits > 3 in 10m.

infra-bot: alert cleared: scratchpool-iops-alert (us-west2) — 1768459402

aj: summary of actions: rolled config back to concurrency=1 (canary -> region), added per-pod io quota, scheduled a canary policy to block big deletions during attach windows, SRE ticket for suspect NVMe. Will follow up with a PR for randomized backoff and batching.

maria: Thanks. please post PR link and timeline here when ready. :thumbsup:

devon: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/janitor/pull/528 (WIP) — adds chunked deletes + backoff.

aj: cc @sre-oncall I will patch kube job to prefer nodes with low writeback next maintenance window.

sre-oncall: ack. watching SMART scan results.

aj: closing thread once PR is merged and canary is promoted in us-west2.

maria: 👍
